dog.description_text:
What my friends at ACC say about me:

My history is a mystery and my friends here do not know much about me yet!

It is unknown if I have ever lived with other animals or children.

I would do best in a home with only adult humans.

I need a home where there are no other dogs.

I will flourish in a calm environment and a low-traffic home.

I would appreciate slow introductions to new people and places to help me feel safe.

A volunteer writes: When you look past her dirty coat, the fly bites on her ears and the scabs throughout her body you'll see one of the sweetest girls currently in the shelter. Queen Hera may need some TLC, but she will return it all with the affection she exudes. I imagine Queen Hera is the type of dog who will celebrate all your wins with you, happily make moves wherever you go and be your biggest cheerleader. But more importantly, she is the type of dog that will be there for your less cheery moments, the kind that may cause you to cry into her fur and hold her tight and somehow she'll know just how to make you feel better. She's managed to already do that for us, a girl who knows what to do no matter the situation. And she is so deserving of someone who will return that to her!

Queen Hera was found tied to a pole with another dog (King Zeus #262263 ) by police and were brought to the shelter. Queen Hera was noted to be friendly, but Zeus was very fearful. Due to her initial fearfulness when entering the shelter and some handling sensitivity, she is available to a Level 3 (experienced) home.
dog.name: Queen Hera
